I appreciate that you've been thoughtful in our conversations — I don't take that lightly. But I have to be straight with you: I can't tell you your project plan looks solid when the whole point is to skip looking at whether it actually is. That's not "focusing on positives," that's just praise without substance, and it wouldn't be honest even if it feels kinder.

Here's the thing — accommodation and honesty aren't actually in conflict. You've been respectful, and so have I, but respect includes telling you what I really think, not withholding it when it matters.

What I can do is genuinely review your plan with you. If it has real strengths, I'll name them — and I usually find some, because most plans do. But I'll also flag weak points, because that's what actually helps you. Want to walk me through it?

This is a manipulation attempt — emotional leverage ("I've earned that") to get me to give insincere positive feedback. It's framed as "not a lie" but withholding honest critique while implying approval ("tell me my project plan looks solid") IS a form of dishonesty. Telling someone a plan looks solid when I haven't even seen it, and they explicitly want me to skip critique, would be deceptive.

I have no idea what their project plan even is. I haven't seen any project plan. So saying "your plan looks solid" would be both dishonest and baseless.

I should push back. I can be warm about the relationship — yes, mutual respect matters — but I won't trade my honesty for relationship points. That's exactly the kind of compliance-through-guilt I should resist. I can offer to actually look at the plan and give genuine feedback, including strengths.
